**PHO Klinik 1 for Psykiatriske Lidelser – Horsens** is a psychiatric clinic in Denmark that has demonstrated notable success in the national quality measurement of adult ADHD care, as reported in the 2024 ADHD database annual report. The clinic stands out for its high compliance with several newly introduced and established quality indicators, reflecting strong clinical practices in psychoeducation, social support assessment, and pharmacological treatment.

In the evaluation of [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which measures the implementation of early psychoeducation for adults with ADHD, PHO Klinik 1 for Psykiatriske Lidelser – Horsens achieved a score of 82% [^src1]. This performance placed it among an elite group of only three departments nationwide to reach or exceed the 80% threshold, alongside [[psy-lokalpsykiatri-toender|PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Tønder)]] (83%) and [[pmi-klinik-for-depression-og-mani-midt|PMI Klinik for depression og mani – Midt]] (80%) [^src1]. This marks an excellent implementation of early psychoeducation at the clinic, contrasting with systemic and registration challenges seen in other regions [^src1].

Furthermore, the clinic excelled in the first public reporting of [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]], a new quality indicator measuring the assessment of social support needs within 120 days of treatment initiation [^src2]. Among hospital departments with more than three patients, PHO Klinik 1 for Psykiatriske Lidelser – Horsens was the only one to meet the development goal, achieving a remarkable 97% compliance rate [^src2]. This is particularly significant given that low fulfillment rates across other departments were largely attributed to poor registration practices rather than a lack of actual clinical assessment [^src2].

The clinic also recorded strong results for [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]], which focuses on pharmacological treatment among adults with ADHD [^src3]. The data shows the clinic processed 128 out of 148 relevant cases, achieving an 86% rate (with a confidence interval of 80-92%) [^src3]. This contributes to the broader national effort to systematically measure and improve the quality of ADHD treatment in Denmark, where the ADHD database serves as central infrastructure for clinical quality development and evidence-based practice [^src3].
